reported.expected: ValueError: Vertex indexes must be in [0; size).
reported.title: add_edge does not validate from_vertex

reported.claim: The recursive result is ignored (`pass` instead of returning False), so a conflicting colouring deeper in the DFS never makes the graph count as non-bipartite.
reported.title: is_bipartite_dfs ignores recursive result

reported.claim: The parent index is computed as floor(i / 2), which gives 1 for index 2 instead of 0; the correct heap parent is (i - 1) // 2.
reported.title: PriorityQueue.par computes wrong heap parent

reported.claim: When exactly two nodes have odd degree the code does `pass` and falls through to return 3, so an Euler path case is reported as not Eulerian; it should return 2.
reported.title: check_circuit_or_path misreports Euler path as not Eulerian

reported.claim: The function returns the count n instead of the computed matching (donor_record or rec_record), so it never reports the stable pairing.
reported.title: stable_matching returns n instead of matching

reported.claim: The first column is updated with `-=` instead of `+=`, so the accumulated path sum down the first column is subtracted rather than added.
reported.title: fill_row subtracts instead of adds on first column

reported.claim: When the capacity is smaller than the first (best-ratio) item's weight, the function returns 0 instead of taking the fraction of that first item that fits.
reported.title: frac_knapsack returns 0 when first item doesn't fit

reported.claim: The slice takes only 31 bits per word (`i : i + 32 - 1`), so to_little_endian receives a 31-char string and raises ValueError, which makes md5_me crash for every message.
reported.expected: A generator yielding one list of 16 integers, each built from a 32-bit word; no exception.
reported.title: get_block_words slices 31 bits, md5 crashes

reported.claim: The left capacity subtracts weights[counter + 1] instead of the current item's weight weights[counter - 1], so it uses the wrong item and goes out of range on the last item.
reported.title: knapsack_recur subtracts wrong item's weight

reported.claim: The off-diagonal sum is accumulated with sign (total -= table[i][j]) instead of absolute values, so a row whose off-diagonal entries are positive can pass the dominance check even when |a_ii| is smaller than the sum of the off-diagonal magnitudes.
reported.expected: A ValueError, since 2 is not greater than |3|.
reported.title: strictly_diagonally_dominant sums signed values instead of absolute

reported.claim: The loop `for row in range(rank)` is fixed at the initial rank, and `rank` is decremented inside the loop, so the loop keeps running past the reduced rank and decrements it again, undercounting the rank.
reported.title: rank_of_matrix loop fixed to initial rank while rank changes

reported.claim: prune builds the list `pruned` of valid candidates but returns the loop variable `item_tuple` instead, so callers receive a tuple (or hit an UnboundLocalError when there are no items) rather than the pruned candidates.
reported.title: prune returns loop variable instead of pruned list

reported.claim: The split error is computed by passing the feature array x instead of the label array y to mean_squared_error (the same mistake recurs on lines 79 and 91), so the split is chosen by feature-value spread rather than label error.
reported.failing_call: DecisionTree(depth=2, min_leaf_size=1).predict... after DecisionTree(depth=2, min_leaf_size=1).train(np.array([1, 2, 3, 4]), np.array([0, 0, 10, 10])); tree.predict(4)
reported.title: DecisionTree.train passes x instead of y to mean_squared_error

reported.claim: inc subtracts num_occur from the count instead of adding it, so repeated transactions reduce node counts (a node reaches 0 after two identical transactions).
reported.title: TreeNode.inc subtracts instead of adds

reported.claim: The vocabulary check uses '>' instead of '>=', so a label equal to vocab_size passes validation and then crashes with an IndexError when building the one-hot filter matrix instead of raising the intended ValueError.
reported.expected: ValueError: Label value must not be greater than vocabulary size.
reported.title: perplexity_loss vocab check off by one

reported.claim: The epsilon is subtracted inside the square root instead of added, so a zero moving average gives a negative argument to math.sqrt and raises ValueError.
reported.title: rmsprop subtracts epsilon inside sqrt

reported.claim: The function returns `side2` instead of the computed Heron's-formula `area`, so the result is just the second side length.
reported.title: area_triangle_three_sides returns side2 instead of area

reported.claim: The trapezoid area takes abs of the sum of the two endpoint values, so a segment where the curve is negative contributes a positive area; it should be (fx2 + fx1) * (x2 - x1) / 2 without abs.
reported.title: area_under_curve trapezoidal_area takes abs of endpoint sum

reported.claim: After trial division, any leftover prime factor greater than 1 is never accounted for in s, so the sum is wrong whenever n has a prime factor larger than sqrt of the reduced value (e.g. n = 2 * 3).
reported.title: sum_of_divisors ignores leftover large prime factor

reported.claim: The origin latitude is read from origin[-1] (the longitude) instead of origin[0], so the wrong start point is used.
reported.title: initial_bearing reads origin latitude from longitude

reported.claim: For a vertical line x = c the returned C is +x instead of -x, which breaks the Ax+By+C=0 convention that segment_intersection relies on (it solves a*x + b*y = -c), so intersections with vertical lines come out wrong.
reported.title: line_coefficients wrong sign of C for vertical lines

reported.claim: The trapezoid term takes abs of the sum of the two endpoint values before multiplying, so segments where the function changes sign contribute positive area and the result is wrong.
reported.title: numerical_integration trapezoidal_area takes abs of endpoint sum

reported.claim: The loop leaves prev_prev_num holding P(n-1), so the function returns the previous Pell number instead of the requested one (should return prev_num).
reported.title: pell_number_iterative returns previous Pell number

reported.claim: The guard `if max_n > 2` should be `>= 2`, so 2 is never yielded when max_n is exactly 2 even though 2 is prime and within the limit.
reported.title: fast_primes omits 2 when max_n is 2

reported.claim: The accumulator starts at 1 instead of 0, so the sum is inflated by 1 and the mean is wrong for every non-empty series.
reported.title: arithmetic_mean accumulator starts at 1

reported.claim: The base case B_0 = 1 is written to the last index (bell[-1]) instead of bell[0], so for max_set_length > 0 the first entry stays 0 and every later Bell number is wrong.
reported.title: bell_numbers writes base case to last index

reported.claim: The loop runs over range(1, number), so it computes the (number-1)th Catalan number instead of the number-th; catalan(2) returns 1 instead of 2.
reported.title: catalan loop range off by one

reported.claim: The split loop stops one digit too early (range upper bound digits - 1 excludes the split where the right part is the last digit), so Kaprekar numbers whose square's split leaves a single leading digit on the left, such as 9 (81 = 8 + 1), are wrongly reported as not Kaprekar.
reported.title: is_kaprekar split loop stops one digit early

reported.claim: The search starts at index 1, so row 0 is never searched and a value present only in the first row is reported as not found.
reported.title: mat_bin_search skips row 0

reported.claim: The empty-input guard uses 'or matrix_b' instead of 'or not matrix_b', so any non-empty matrix_b returns [] instead of the Kronecker product.
reported.title: kronecker_product empty guard missing `not`

reported.claim: After each row, next_row is assigned the same list object as current_row instead of a copy, so the diagonal read next_row[col+1] sees values already overwritten in the current row, giving an overestimated square size.
reported.title: space-optimized largest square aliases row lists instead of copying

reported.claim: The dimension check calls _verify_matrix_sizes, which requires both matrices to have identical shapes, so compatible but non-identical matrix products (e.g. 2x3 times 3x1) are rejected with a broadcast error instead of being multiplied.
reported.title: multiply requires identical shapes instead of compatible

reported.claim: Using true division instead of floor division makes leap_day_reinstall_number fractional, so the calendar arithmetic gives wrong dates for centuries not divisible by 4.
reported.title: gauss_easter uses true division instead of floor division

reported.claim: The main loop stops at len(sorted_points) - 1 (exclusive), so the last sorted point is never considered and can be dropped from the hull.
reported.title: graham_scan loop skips last sorted point

reported.claim: The function divides by molar_mass instead of multiplying, so m2 = m1 * (r1/r2)^2 is computed as (r1/r2)^2 / m1. The doctest value 1.970351 encodes this same error.
reported.title: second_molar_mass divides instead of multiplies

reported.claim: The check `tangential_force <= 0` rejects a zero tangential force, so the `elif tangential_force == 0` branch that computes the tangential force is unreachable; it should only reject negative values.
reported.title: shear_stress rejects zero tangential force, making branch unreachable

reported.claim: When a process arrives after the current time, the clock is advanced by adding the arrival time to the current time instead of setting it to the arrival time, which overstates the elapsed time.
reported.title: MLFQ.round_robin advances clock by adding arrival time

reported.claim: For full groups the code takes the median of the whole tail arr[i:] instead of the five-element group arr[i:i+5], so the group medians are wrong whenever the input has more than 10 elements.
reported.title: median_of_medians uses whole tail instead of 5-element group

reported.claim: The n <= 1 guard uses 'pass' instead of returning, so for an empty list block_size is 0 and range(0, 0, 0) raises ValueError.
reported.title: kirkpatrick_reisch_sort n<=1 guard uses pass, empty list raises ValueError

reported.claim: The zeros bucket is recursed with bit_position + 1 instead of moving down to the next lower bit, so the bit position never reaches 0 and recursion does not terminate for lists whose zero-bucket still has several elements.
reported.title: _msd_radix_sort recurses zeros bucket with bit_position+1

reported.claim: The swap test compares collection[i - 1] with collection[i] but then swaps i and i + 1, so it compares the wrong pair and the list is not fully sorted.
reported.title: odd_even_transposition compares wrong pair than it swaps

reported.claim: The length test is joined with 'or' instead of 'and', so any 13-digit number is reported valid without checking the check digit.
reported.title: barcode is_valid uses `or` so 13-digit numbers always valid

reported.claim: The early return uses `m >= len(text)`, so a pattern that exactly equals the whole text is reported as not found, though it should match at index 0.
reported.title: bitap_string_match misses pattern equal to whole text

reported.claim: When the weighted subtotal is divisible by 10 the checksum becomes 10 instead of 0, so a valid PESEL whose check digit is 0 is rejected.
reported.title: is_polish_national_id checksum 10 instead of 0

reported.claim: The swap guard uses `<=` instead of `<`, so two words of equal length swap and recurse forever, causing a RecursionError instead of returning the distance.
reported.title: levenshtein_distance_optimized infinite recursion for equal-length words

reported.claim: The function returns the leftover loop variable `word` (a string) instead of the `occurrence` dictionary of counts.
reported.title: word_occurrence returns loop variable instead of dictionary
